roast.fullContent: Lisa Cotton, the Independent with a knack for dodging the spotlight, is chucking her hat in the ring with a policy mix that’s as clear as mud. She’s vaguely progressive on social services—good on ya for caring, Lisa—but swings hard right on family and national security, probably dreaming of border walls and 1950s family dinners. Her “people over planet” mantra is a right kick in the guts to the environment, leaving greenies like Sophie Scamps choking on their kale smoothies, especially since Lisa’s slapped Scamps dead last on her preferences behind even the Liberals. With a past as a parliament staffer and a chaplaincy gig, she’s got a Christian worldview guiding her, but her website’s as empty as a pub on a Monday morning. Her corflutes are popping up like weeds, but with no real achievements or detailed plans, it’s hard to know if she’s a serious contender or just here to stir the pot.

roast.fullContent: Right, let’s have a bit of a laugh at Amber Robertson from the Trumpet of Patriots party, running in Mackellar for the 2025 federal election. With bugger all info out there on this mystery candidate, we can only assume Amber’s either hiding under a rock or too busy blowing their own trumpet to share any actual policies on healthcare, education, or climate change. roast.fullContent: Sophie Scamps, the Teal Independent MP for Mackellar, is the self-proclaimed saviour of Sydney’s northern beaches, having booted out the Libs in 2022 with her progressive, community-hugging vibe. A doctor with a fancy degree, she’s banging on about climate change like it’s the end of the world—fair dinkum, we get it, the planet’s hot, but does every speech need to sound like a doomsday sermon? She’s also pushing tax cuts for small biz, which is a fair go, but let’s see if that’s just a sweetener to mask her knack for defending her Teal mates in every scandal going—Monique, Allegra, Nicolette, she’s got their backs like a loyal kelpie. Always at local forums spruiking her grassroots guff, Sophie’s the ultimate “I’m one of you” pollies, but whether she’s more than just a teal-tinted protest vote remains to be seen come 2025.

roast.content: Jeffrey Quinn, Labor’s hopeful for Mackellar, is banging on about fixing up healthcare with bulk-billed GPs and a fancy new Urgent Care Clinic in Dee Why, all part of a whopping $8.5 billion Medicare splurge—reckon he thinks he’s Santa Claus with stethoscopes. He’s also spruiking tax cuts for all and sundry to ease the cost of living, while promising to keep inflation from going full Mad Max again. On the infrastructure front, he’s all about zero-emission buses and shiny new roads like Mona Vale and Wakehurst Parkway, as if turning the Northern Beaches into some eco-utopia will win him votes.
